title: reduce-streaming-token-latency-adaptive-flush-backpressure-kernel-scheduling-kv-cache-batching
author: Priya Nair
body:
Motivation: Streaming token generation latency spikes during high-concurrency workloads were traced to three interacting causes: synchronous token-flush cadence that waits for fixed time windows, token-loop backpressure amplification when a stalled consumer blocks other inflight streams, and suboptimal kernel scheduling that delayed small, low-latency dispatches. This PR implements an adaptive flush cadence, per-stream backpressure isolation and early-drain heuristics, coordinated with updated kernel scheduling priorities and KV-cache hotkey hints to reduce tail token latency while preserving throughput.

Summary of changes: 1) Adaptive flush cadence: replace fixed flush timers with an adaptive controller that flushes partial tokens earlier when per-stream queue latency exceeds a target; controller uses EWMA on per-stream enqueue latency and global occupancy to decide flush thresholds. 2) Backpressure isolation: token-loop now maintains per-client logical windows and applies early-drop/priority escalation for stalled consumers; this prevents a single slow consumer from stalling the shared dispatch loop. 3) Kernel scheduling priority: add lightweight priority tagging for small, interactive streams; scheduler prefers low-latency kernels for tagged dispatches and falls back to high-throughput kernels for bulk batches. 4) KV-cache hotkey hints: runtime emits hotkey hints for recently accessed KV slices so the cache manager keeps hot regions resident, reducing cache load for streaming workloads. 5) Continuous batching improvements: dynamic batch consolidation respects priority tags and can form hybrid batches that mix low-latency singletons with throughput batches when hardware permits.

Implementation notes: All changes are behind a runtime feature flag (streaming_latency_opt_v2) and guarded with runtime knobs: adaptive_flush_window_ms, per_stream_window_size, priority_escalation_threshold. The main runtime loop changes are confined to runtime/streaming/token_loop.rs and runtime/scheduler/scheduler.rs. KV cache hints are added in runtime/kv_cache/hints.rs with fallbacks if the cache manager is not enabled.

Testing and benchmarks: Unit and integration tests updated for new controller heuristics and priority behavior. Benchmark harness (perf-canary) runs were executed across RTX and A100 shapes. Observed improvements: median token emission latency down 48% and P99 down 60% for interactive workloads at 1k RPS per GPU on our internal benchmark suite. End-to-end throughput unchanged within 3% on batch-heavy workloads. See the benchmark summary section below.

Checklist: 
- [x] Feature-flag guarded
- [x] Unit tests covering controller heuristics and priority escalation
- [x] Integration tests for backpressure isolation
- [x] Perf benchmarks added to perf-canary
- [x] Documentation updated (runtime config docs)

Risk and mitigation: The adaptive flush controller could increase small write amplification and slightly raise GPU kernel dispatch rate; mitigated by rate caps and a conservative default config. Changes are gated by feature flag and allowed to be toggled per-cluster. Rollback is a single runtime flag flip to restore previous behavior.

Related: follow-up work tracked under ENG-8940 to expose per-tenant knobs in Dedicated and ENG-9011 to add telemetry for adaptive controller decisions.

Detailed commit and file-level summary, CI, reviews, and benchmarks included in PR metadata below.
commits: a1f4d2c feat(streaming): adaptive flush controller and heuristics
b3c7e9d fix(kv-cache): add hotkey hint emission and safe fallbacks
c2b9f0a perf(scheduler): priority tagging for low-latency kernels
d4e1b7a test(streaming): add integration tests for backpressure isolation
e5f2a3b docs(runtime): document streaming_latency_opt_v2 knobs and defaults
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Overall looks good, biggest question is around the default EWMA window - can we make it more conservative?
Priya Nair: Updated EWMA window default to 100ms and made it configurable via adaptive_flush_window_ms (added unit test).
Marisol Vega: Please add a gate in scheduler to avoid priority tagging for models that explicitly opted out (done).
Liam Patel: CI flaky on integration test, re-ran and added additional stabilization (increased test timeout and synthetic consumer pacing).
Ethan Cole: Approved after addressing default config and test stabilization.
benchmarks: interactive workload (1k RPS/GPU): median token latency 85ms -> 44ms (-48%)
interactive workload (1k RPS/GPU): P99 token latency 340ms -> 136ms (-60%)
throughput workload (batch-heavy): tokens/sec change within +3% (no regression)
GPU utilization: unchanged at target operating point due to hybrid batching
release_notes: Reduced streaming token latency via adaptive flush cadence, backpressure isolation, priority kernel scheduling, and KV-cache hotkey hints. No breaking changes; feature gated behind streaming_latency_opt_v2.
risk: Medium - introduces more aggressive flush behavior and scheduler prioritization that could increase dispatch rate. Mitigated by feature flag and conservative defaults.
rollback_plan: Disable runtime feature flag streaming_latency_opt_v2 and revert priority tagging via runtime knob; monitoring dashboard added to detect regressions to trigger rollback.
notes: Deployed to canary and observed stable improvements; will roll to production in a staged rollout with A/B and canary checks.
Follow-up work: ENG-9011 telemetry, ENG-9120 per-tenant knobs for Dedicated.
